formats.key: send((uint32 dstEid, bytes32 to, uint256 amountLD, uint256 minAmountLD, bytes extraOptions, bytes composeMsg, bytes oftCmd) _sendParam, (uint256 nativeFee, uint256 lzTokenFee) _fee, address _refundAddress)
effects: Takes amountLD FXRP from the signer into the adapter with safeTransferFrom. This spends the signer's FXRP allowance to the adapter (OFTAdapterFeeUpgradeable._debit).
The recipient `to` on chain dstEid is credited amountLD minus the Flare BPS fee, rounded down to remove dust. The call reverts if that is below minAmountLD (_debitView, SlippageExceeded).
The fee and dust stay locked in the adapter as feeBalance, which the owner can withdraw.
Exactly nativeFee in FLR must be sent as msg.value (_payNative reverts otherwise). It is paid to the LayerZero endpoint, which refunds any excess to _refundAddress.
If lzTokenFee > 0, the LZ token is taken from the signer for the endpoint (_payLzToken). The descriptor forces this value to 0.

If composeMsg is not empty, the message becomes SEND_AND_CALL and the destination calls `to` with composeMsg after crediting it. extraOptions set destination gas and options, such as native drops paid from nativeFee.
The call reverts if `to` is zero or does not match the address format of the destination peer (RecipientChecking.checkRecipient).
formats.shown: Intent 'Bridge FXRP', with the FXRP amount sent, the minimum FXRP received, the destination chain name, the raw bytes32 recipient, the FLR bridge fee and the refund address.

findings.title: send: the intent 'Bridge FXRP' gives no amount, destination or recipient, and there is no interpolatedIntent.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: "intent": "Bridge FXRP", no interpolatedIntent. The amount, dstEid and recipient appear only in the fields.
findings.fix: Add "interpolatedIntent": "Bridge {_sendParam.amountLD} to {_sendParam.dstEid}" (the amount and the destination enum).

findings.title: send: composeMsg is visible: never, but a non-empty one makes the destination call the recipient with hidden data.
findings.evidence: OFTCoreUpgradeable._buildMsgAndOptions: msgType = hasCompose ? SEND_AND_CALL : SEND. _lzReceive encodes _message.composeMsg() for lzCompose on `to`. descriptor.json: composeMsg has "visible": "never". When `to` is a composer, what happens to the credited FXRP depends on bytes the signer never sees.
findings.fix: Use "visible": {"mustMatch": ["0x"]} for composeMsg, or show it when it is not empty.

findings.title: send: extraOptions is visible: never, but it can direct part of the shown bridge fee to native drops on the destination.
findings.evidence: OFTCoreUpgradeable._buildMsgAndOptions: options = combineOptions(_sendParam.dstEid, msgType, _sendParam.extraOptions). The options go to endpoint.send with nativeFee (OAppSenderUpgradeable._lzSend). descriptor.json: extraOptions has "visible": "never".
findings.fix: Show extraOptions when it is not empty, or note that the bridge fee may include destination gas or native drops.

findings.title: send: the recipient is shown as a raw bytes32 with 24 leading zero hex digits.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: #._sendParam.to has "format": "raw". Case 0 shows Recipient '0x0000000000000000000000001111111111111111111111111111111111111111'. Every enum destination is EVM, and RecipientChecking makes EVM recipients left-padded.
findings.fix: For the EVM destinations, show `#._sendParam.to.[12:32]` as addressName. Keep raw only if non-EVM peers such as Solana must be supported.

findings.title: send: the Flare system fee kept from the amount is read from storage and not shown, only bounded by the minimum to receive.
findings.evidence: OFTAdapterFeeUpgradeable._debitView: fee = getFee(_dstEid, _amountLD), then amountReceivedLD = _removeDust(_amountLD - fee), and the call reverts if that is below _minAmountLD. The fee goes to feeBalance. The screen shows 'Amount to send' and 'Minimum to receive', and the code enforces the minimum.
findings.fix: None needed. A label such as 'Minimum to receive (after Flare fee)' would explain the gap.

findings.title: send: the destination enum lists only four endpoint IDs, so any other configured peer shows as a raw number.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json metadata.enums.destination lists only 30101, 30102, 30184 and 30375. Peers are set in storage (peers(_dstEid)) and cannot be checked here.
findings.fix: Add every endpoint ID that the adapter has a peer for.
